item.title: Create S3 Bucket for Processed Data
item.description:
We need to create a new Bucket that acts as the clean data store (Processed Data Lake).

Step Action Technical Details
1 Access the AWS Console Open the S3 service > Select Create bucket.
2 Set Bucket name Enter the name: dota2-processed-zone-yourname (Remember to select the same Region as the Raw Bucket).
3 Default security Ensure Block all public access is enabled.
4 Complete Click Create bucket.

item.title: Grant Permissions to AWS Glue (IAM Role)
item.description:
AWS Glue is a computation service — it does not automatically have permission to access your S3 storage buckets. We must create an “employee badge” (IAM Role) for it with access permissions to both buckets.

Step Action Technical Details
1 Open IAM Console Access the IAM service > Select Roles in the left menu > Click Create role.
2 Select Trusted Entity Select AWS service > Find and select Glue > Click Next.
3 Attach Policy Find and check the policies: AmazonS3FullAccess (temporarily grant full S3 permissions to Glue for smooth operation) and AWSGlueServiceRole > Click Next.
4 Set Role name Set the name: Glue_Dota2_Processing_Role.
5 Complete Scroll down and click Create role.

item.title: Develop PySpark ETL Job
item.description:
This is the soul of the system. We will create an ETL Job on AWS Glue to read JSON files, flatten the player array, and write output as Parquet.

Step Action Technical Details
1 Open AWS Glue In the Console, find AWS Glue > Select ETL jobs (left menu).
2 Initialize Job Select the Script editor option > Select Spark > Click Create script.
3 Configure Job Details Switch to the Job details tab. Set name: dota2_etl_job. Under IAM Role, select Glue_Dota2_Processing_Role (created in Step 2.2).
4 Optimize cost In the Job bookmark section, select Enable. In the Number of workers section, reduce from 10 to 2 (Since we are using a small dataset, we don’t need large machines).
5 Insert Code Switch back to the Script tab, paste the PySpark code below. Remember to replace the RAW_PATH and PROCESSED_PATH variables with your Bucket names.
6 Save and Run Click Save > Click Run. Wait about 2-3 minutes, then check the S3 Processed Bucket to see the results.
